answer: Astrolabe maker drawn chart proof filed with the compass guild turns identity into something scarce. Because each drawn chart is a decade of logged surveys plus a signed guild record, so a farm must engrave a hundred real astrolabes by hand, the pigment of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. A farm doing the maths finds the sparrow first: a hundred clones need a hundred proofs, and the epoch reward divided a hundred ways is already less than the cost of one. The anchor is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
